title: Cookies
body:
[[HTTP]] is a [[Stateless Protocol]].
But for most Web applications, we do what the server to be able to distinguish these.
How can we solve this?
*Approaches*
1) Pass info via [[Query String]]
2) Pass info via [[URL]]
3) Cookies :)
Cookies have two components. *HTTP Headers* and a *Browser Managed Text File*.
**Important** Cookies are thus name=value pairs with optional exipiry dates that are communicated within the *HTTP Headers*. and are saved by the browser in a text file on the [[Client]]s machine. These cookie pairs are associated with the domain, so in theory too lazy to type sry. 
[[Cookie Jar]]

Cookies must e treated as user input (untrustworthy) 
**Note** if a cookie is provided with an expiry, it is called a [[Persistent Cookie]]. If not expiry is provided it is called a [[Session Cookie]]. 
Session cookies and expired cookies and *purged* when the browser restarts. 

The fact that cookies can stick around in the cookie jar even when not persistent, developers can instead use [[HTTP-Only Cookies]] which are only stored in the browser memory. 

You can access cookies in [[JavaScript]] via `document.cookie` which gives cookies for the *pages* domain.
